questions.stem: These left ventricular pressure-volume loops compare a control loop with altered loops. What does the leftward shift of the end-systolic point along the steeper dashed line in the right panel primarily represent?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased afterload with reduced stroke volume

explanation.summary: The end-systolic pressure-volume relationship (ESPVR) line steepens with increased contractility, allowing the ventricle to eject to a smaller end-systolic volume at any given pressure, independent of loading conditions.
explanation.whyCorrect: The end-systolic pressure-volume relationship (ESPVR) line steepens with increased contractility, allowing the ventricle to eject to a smaller end-systolic volume at any given pressure, independent of loading conditions.

questions.stem: This diagram shows oxygen consumption measured at the mouth, pulmonary artery saturation of 75%, and arterial saturation of 95%. Which method of determining cardiac output does it illustrate?

explanation.summary: The Fick principle calculates cardiac output by dividing whole-body oxygen consumption (VO2) by the arteriovenous oxygen content difference, here estimated from the mixed venous (PA, 75%) versus arterial (95%) saturations.
explanation.whyCorrect: The Fick principle calculates cardiac output by dividing whole-body oxygen consumption (VO2) by the arteriovenous oxygen content difference, here estimated from the mixed venous (PA, 75%) versus arterial (95%) saturations.

questions.stem: An indicator is injected at a venous site and sampled from an artery, producing the concentration-versus-time curve shown, including a second smaller hump requiring extrapolation. What is that second hump, and why must it be excluded?

choices.label: C
choices.text: A second bolus given to confirm the reading

choices.label: D
choices.text: A calibration artifact that is added back to the curve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recirculation of indicator, which is excluded by extrapolating the downslope to avoid overestimating flow

explanation.summary: In indicator-dilution measurement of cardiac output, dye recirculates back to the sampling site before it fully clears; the primary washout curve is extrapolated exponentially so recirculated indicator does not falsely lower the calculated mean concentration and inflate estimated flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: In indicator-dilution measurement of cardiac output, dye recirculates back to the sampling site before it fully clears; the primary washout curve is extrapolated exponentially so recirculated indicator does not falsely lower the calculated mean concentration and inflate estimated flow.
